problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{x-{y}^{2}}.$ The partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ is given by

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\frac{h(x,y)}{{(x-{y}^{2})}^{2}}.
$$

Find the function $h(x,y).$

feedback.problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=\frac{3x+y}{\sqrt{x+y}}.$ The partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ is given by

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{h(x,y)}{2(x+y)\sqrt{x+y}}.
$$

Find the function $h(x,y).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

Using the quotient and chain rules, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{3x+y}{\sqrt{x+y}}) \\  & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂x}(3x+y)\cdot \sqrt{x+y}-(3x+y)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{x+y})}{{(\sqrt{x+y})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(3\cdot \sqrt{x+y}-(3x+y)\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+y}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x+y))}{{(\sqrt{x+y})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(3\cdot \sqrt{x+y}-(3x+y)\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+y}}\cdot 1)}{{(\sqrt{x+y})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{6(x+y)-(3x+y)}{2\sqrt{x+y}})}{x+y} \\  & =\frac{3x+5y}{2(x+y)\sqrt{x+y}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
h(x,y)=3x+5y.
$$
